lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Paulownia as a modern family split from old Scrophulariaceae using tree habit, enormous opposite leaves, woody capsule and masses of winged seeds.

project_scope.note: The sole project species is accepted but native to East Asia and introduced in Texas. This is a crew/invasive-lookalike family lesson, not a native anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a fast-growing tree with enormous opposite cordate leaves and terminal panicles of large lavender tubular flowers. Confirm persistent woody capsules packed with thousands of tiny winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Trees or woody plants; Paulownia has very large opposite cordate leaves, often densely hairy beneath.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Large bisexual tubular/campanulate 5-lobed flowers in terminal panicles; stamens epipetalous; ovary superior.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Woody 2-valved capsule containing very numerous tiny multi-winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Huge opposite heart-shaped leaves + lavender spring flower panicles + persistent woody seed capsules = Paulowniaceae/Paulownia.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: giant opposite leaf → lavender terminal panicle → woody capsule → winged seed → old Scrophulariaceae split
visual_lesson.intro: Paulownia is an excellent taxonomy-and-field combination: once a scroph in older treatments, now easy to remember as its own woody Lamiales family.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the enormous opposite leaf
steps.look_for: Very large heart-shaped leaves in opposite pairs, often velvety beneath.
steps.why_it_matters: The leaf size and arrangement are an immediate field clue even without flowers.

steps.title: 2 · Find the terminal lavender flower panicle
steps.look_for: Large erect clusters of lavender-blue tubular/campanulate flowers, often appearing before full leaf-out.
steps.why_it_matters: This ties the tree to the fused-corolla Lamiales pattern.

steps.title: 3 · Open the woody capsule
steps.look_for: Pointed woody 2-valved capsules that can remain on the tree after leaf fall.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit is much more diagnostic than generic purple flower color.

steps.title: 4 · Look at the tiny winged seeds
steps.look_for: Numerous tiny flat seeds with conspicuous membranous wings.
steps.why_it_matters: Seed structure is one of the strongest visible characters supporting Paulowniaceae.

comparisons.title: Paulowniaceae vs Scrophulariaceae
comparisons.rule: Paulownia is now separated from Scrophulariaceae. Its tree habit, giant opposite cordate leaves, woody capsule and masses of tiny winged seeds make the project species distinctive.

comparisons.title: Paulowniaceae vs Bignoniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be woody Lamiales with large tubular flowers and winged seeds. Paulownia has huge opposite simple cordate leaves and compact woody capsules; many Bignoniaceae have compound leaves or vines and long bivalved capsules.

visual_lesson.caveat: The project species Paulownia tomentosa is introduced in Texas; family recognition does not imply native restoration value.

genera.fast_cue: tree + enormous opposite cordate leaves + lavender panicles + woody capsule with many winged seeds

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show seed body and multiple thin wings
scale leaf against hand/twig without relying on size alone
compact woody capsule vs long bivalved capsule
